thread.title: Indonesia Bourse May See Continued Strength On Friday

title: Indonesia Bourse May See Continued Strength On Friday
text:
Indonesia Bourse May See Continued Strength On Friday September 27, 2018, 10:00: The Indonesia stock market on Thursday snapped the three-day slide in which it had surrendered almost 85 points or 1.3 percent. The Jakarta Composite Index now rests just beneath the 5,930-point plateau and it may add to its winnings on Friday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is firm, with support expected from the oil and technology stocks. The European and U.S. markets were up and the Asian bourses are tipped to follow suit.
The JCI finished modestly higher on Thursday as the financial shares and resource stocks were mostly in the green.
For the day, the index climbed 55.94 points or 0.95 percent to finish at 5,929.22 after trading between 5,870.54 and 5,931.72. There were 185 gainers and 156 decliners, with 150 stocks finishing unchanged.
Among the actives, Voksel Electric soared 3.95 percent, while Lotte Chemical shed 0.71 percent, SLJ Global jumped 1.96 percent, Jasa Marga climbed 1.82 percent, Bank Pan Indonesia skidded 1.04 percent, XL Axiata added 0.36 percent, Bank Danamon Indonesia collected 0.70 percent, Bank Central Asia lost 0.83 percent, Bank Mandiri gained 0.38 percent, Bank Negara Indonesia picked up 0.34 percent, Bank Rakyat Indonesia spiked 2.68 percent, Indosat advanced 0.67 percent, Bumi Resources tumbled 1.83 percent, Vale Indonesia was up 0.27 percent, Aneka Tambang surged 3.73 percent and Bank MNC Internasional and Bukit Darmo Property were unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is upbeat as stocks opened higher on Thursday. They faded slightly in the afternoon but still finished firmly in the green.
The Dow added 54.65 points or 0.21 percent to 26,439.93, while the NASDAQ gained 51.60 points or 0.65 percent to 8,041.97 and the S&P was up 8.03 points or 0.28 percent to 2,914.00.
A notable advance by shares of Apple (AAPL) contributed to the higher close on Wall Street after J.P. Morgan initiated coverage of the company's stock with an Overweight rating.
In economic news, the Commerce Department noted a bigger than expected jump in durable goods orders in August. The Commerce Department also said the pace of U.S. economic growth in the second quarter was unrevised at 4.2 percent from the previous estimate.
Also, the Labor Department noted a rebound in initial jobless claims in the week ended September 22. And the National Association of Realtors said pending home sales dropped much more than expected in August.
Crude oil prices moved higher on Thursday, amid concerns that sanctions on Iran from November may result in supply shortage in the market. Crude oil futures for November delivery ended up $0.55 or 0.8 percent at $72.12 a barrel. //www.rttnews.com/2938886/indonesia-bourse-may-see-continued-strength-on-friday.aspx
